summary.title: Mike Acton's Expectations of Professional Software Engineers
summary.one_liner: A written-up checklist of about 50 habits Mike Acton expects from professional software engineers, covering problem definition, planning, data and performance awareness, hardware targets, and professional conduct.
takeaways: Be able to state precisely what problem you are solving, why it matters, and how much effort it is worth.
Always have a Plan B, ideally implemented early, and know the steps, unknowns, and completion test for your current problem.
Understand the data: real values, acceptable ranges, change frequency, input likelihood, and how it is laid out in memory.
Profile performance and memory regularly, use more than one profiling tool, and know the hardware your software targets.
Communicate early about conflicts and blockers, avoid wasting others' time, and take feedback seriously.
summary.summary: The article expands on a 2019 talk by games industry veteran Mike Acton, in which he listed about 50 things he expects of the developers he works with, framed as a tongue-in-cheek firing offence. The author rewrites each point as a self-check statement (for example, "I can articulate precisely what problem I am trying to solve") and adds an explanation, examples, and related quotes. The points span problem definition, planning and risk, data and memory layout, latency and throughput, profiling, hardware targets, debugging production, and professional conduct. It is a reading list of opinions rather than a tutorial, and the author notes it is not specific to games.
